newsitem.title: USA: Alleged NYC immigration fraud ring busted.
newsitem.headline: Alleged NYC immigration fraud ring busted.

text.p: Authorities said on Thursday seven people had been arrested for allegedly defrauding recent immigrants of thousands of dollars by selling phony residency documents, working papers or American brides.

In a four-month investigation dubbed "Operation Green Card," undercover agents acted on tips that fake documents were being sold in New York City's Brooklyn borough, mostly to recent Caribbean immigrants, said officials with the Brooklyn District Attorney's rackets bureau.
Undercover purchases led the agents to a Brooklyn-based company called International Business Consultants, that called itself an immigration consulting agency, they said.
The company offered an array of services, almost all of them illegal, to immigrants, said Dennis Hawkins, chief of the rackets bureau.
The company sold fake resident alien cards, known as green cards, for $400, he said.
Hundreds of recent immigrants may have been duped. While many immigrants knew they were buying bogus documents, many probably did not realise the green cards were fake, he said.
Some 1.5 million Brooklyn residents have roots in the Caribbean, the district attorney's office said.
For $4,000, the company offered an undercover investigator an Americam woman as a bride, Hawkins said. Marrying a U.S. citizen would give an illegal alien resident status, he said.
For $5,000, the company offered to help immigrants apply for legal green cards, he said.
Legally, that process entails only a minimal application fee.
A search of the company's files turned up fake birth certificates and other papers the company allegedly used to file for green cards, Hawkins said.
Company president Evan Campbell, also known as Charles Morris, Joan Graham and three other alleged street-level green-card dealers were arrested, he said.
Campbell and Graham were charged with conspiracy and forgery and, if convicted, face up to seven years in prison for each green card sold.
